AgentKnowledgeBindingV1.description: Immutable, server-enforced knowledge scope available to an Agent. Provider selection and any provider-specific namespace restriction are intentionally absent from the model-facing tool schema, so a tool call cannot widen the template's knowledge boundary.

parallelToolCallsMigrated.description: One-time settings migration marker. Older desktop builds persisted `parallelToolCalls: false` as their UI default, so absence means those values have not yet been upgraded to the runtime's default-on policy.

BrowserContent.description: Content that can later be passed straight into a multimodal tool-result/message contract.

CapabilityProjection.description: A deterministic, fail-closed view of the capabilities available to one Agent execution. `allow_all_*` is explicit so a missing field never means unrestricted access when an ExecutionContext is deserialized.

CellRange.description: An inclusive range using zero-based coordinates.

CodexAccountStatus.description:
Public account controls for the local Codex App Server.

The server owns the child process and keeps authentication inside Codex. OpenTopia only exposes non-secret account metadata and the documented login instructions to its UI.

oneOf.description: The current final candidate must be rejected and returned to the model.
The turn may finish; the signal is only surfaced as a reminder.

accessibilityTree.description: Reserved for a future UIA adapter. It is omitted rather than fabricating accessibility data.

captureRect.description: Coordinates in computer actions are relative to this image, never to CSS/DIP coordinates.

credentialRef.description: Opaque reference resolved by a credential provider. Never a token or password.

ConnectionBindingV1.description: Pins one account-level Connection and the immutable capability revision that was reviewed when an Agent template was published.

annotations.description: Only standard, public MCP behavior hints are projected here.

ContextAuthority.description:
Semantic authority carried by a context item before a provider adapter maps it to the provider's supported message roles.

This is harness metadata. Providers never receive this enum as a prompt tag. `Data` means the item is asserted as context or state, but does not mint new instructions merely because its transport role may be `developer`.

ContextCheckpointPhase.description:
One evidence-backed stage in the task's durable history.

`from_seq`/`through_seq` are the authoritative ordering keys. Timestamps are canonicalized from those events by the checkpoint service rather than trusted from model output.

inputTokens.description: Local estimate of the logical agent request before compaction.

postCompactionTokens.description: Local estimate after the checkpoint starts a new request epoch. The provider-reported result is only available after that request finishes.

providerInputTokens.description: Provider-reported usage for the auxiliary compaction model call.

remainingPercent.description: Percentage of the original request remaining after compaction.

oneOf.description: Legacy serialized kind retained for replay compatibility. New contexts use `CapabilityCatalog` or `SkillInstructions` instead.

ContextLifecycle.description:
Semantic lifetime used by the harness for auditing and invalidation.

This is intentionally independent from `ContextCacheScope`: a Skill chosen for one Turn may still be placed in a reusable provider prefix, while a durable checkpoint belongs to an Epoch even when transported in that same prefix. Providers never receive this enum as a prompt tag.

enabled.description: Deployment-owned gate. It is intentionally not writable through the settings API, so a consumer session cannot enable enterprise surfaces.

ExecutionConnectionOperationV1.description: Credential-free operation route frozen into an Agent instance. The runtime must still revalidate the live Connection and fingerprint immediately before crossing the external-call boundary.

resource.description: A workspace-relative root, network origin, or logical database route.

oneOf.description: The event remains immutable for audit, but a newer invocation replaces it and is the only copy that may be started.

connectionAuthority.description: Immutable operation-level authority captured when the Run starts. `None` is reserved for persisted runs created before this field existed; those are restored through explicit legacy-projection inference.

ingressTrigger.description: The ingress source that created this Run. It is persisted separately from the raw `input` so the active Flow can target any configured node Trigger without mutating its immutable Revision.

outputReviewRequired.description: Active Flows pause after terminal output until a HumanTask records the review decision. Trial/manual compatibility runs may opt out.

state.description: Reducer-owned shared state. Node outputs remain the immutable routing source; state channels are applied only at a committed superstep.

KnowledgeLibraryProviderV1.description: Knowledge retrieval backend selected by an Agent template. The provider is part of the immutable Agent version; provider-owned databases and indexes remain deployment configuration rather than template identity.

_meta.description: Provider-owned extension metadata from the MCP tool's `_meta` field. OpenTopia only acts on explicitly namespaced contracts it understands.

oneOf.description: A Plan-mode proposal extracted from the model's `<proposed_plan>` block. This is presentation content, not the executable WorkForm maintained by the Default/Goal `update_plan` tool.

inline.description: Whether the user placed this source at this exact position in the request. Legacy and context-only sources remain trailing parts.

library_provider.description: Optional per-Turn retrieval backend selected by the conversation UI. This is execution metadata only; model history projection omits the TurnContext part itself.

ModelContentPart.description:
A typed unit of model input or tool output.

Text is the portable baseline for providers and tools, while the other variants retain information that would otherwise be flattened into a prompt string. `Image` stores the original bytes so provider adapters can choose their native multimodal representation at the last possible point.

role.description: Provider transport role. Semantic authority is tracked separately so contextual data can be carried in a developer-shaped envelope without being classified as a developer-authored rule.

chatMessageProtocol.description: Assistant-message replay requirements discovered for Chat Completions.

chatReasoningProtocol.description: Reasoning request envelope proven together with the Chat function-tool round trip. `None` is reserved for reports written before v7.

chatStreamingTools.description: Chat Completions function calls remain structurally valid when tool arguments are delivered as a stream. This is negotiated separately from non-streaming function support because compatible relays frequently use different translation paths for the two transports.

chatStrictFunctionTools.description: Chat Completions function tools with provider-enforced strict JSON Schema output. This is negotiated independently from ordinary function tools because many compatible relays accept `tools` but reject `strict`.

responsesApplyPatch.description: The named Responses `apply_patch` tool and its structured call/output item pair. This is negotiated per endpoint/model, never inferred from a vendor or model-name table.

responsesCustomTools.description: Freeform/custom tool definitions and `custom_tool_call` output items.

responsesFunctionTools.description: Function tools using the Responses wire shape. Kept separate from `responses_native_tools`: a relay may accept hosted web search while rejecting application-defined functions, or vice versa.

responsesReasoningProtocol.description: Reasoning request envelope proven together with the Responses function-tool round trip. `None` is reserved for legacy reports.

responsesStreamingTools.description: Responses tool calls remain structurally valid over the streaming event protocol used by the runtime.

responsesStrictFunctionTools.description: Responses function tools with provider-enforced strict JSON Schema output. Kept separate from the portable function-tool capability.

OperationGrantV1.description: Grants one stable provider operation. The operation ID is deliberately not a runtime tool name; the server resolves it through the pinned capability revision before execution.

oneOf.description:
Unrestricted host access with destructive actions still reviewed.

This preserves the behavior of the original `full_access` preset.
Unrestricted host access with approval requests disabled.

PreviewCapabilities.description: Operations granted to a resolved resource. Renderers consume these capabilities instead of inferring authority from where a file came from.

oneOf.description: GPT-5.6 and later: cache only prefixes ending at explicit breakpoints.
Earlier models: keep the prompt cache in volatile memory.
Earlier models that support extended retention.

ProviderAdapterKind.description: Wire protocol selected for one concrete endpoint/model pair. Connections are credentials and routing; adapters are protocol codecs, so one relay may legitimately select different adapters for different models.

ProviderAdapterProfile.description: Normalized output of provider capability negotiation. Probe diagnostics may remain provider-specific, but the runtime consumes only this stable adapter contract and therefore never needs to reinterpret a probe response.

ProviderCacheTrace.description: Describes the exact structured input sent by a provider adapter using only hashes, safe field names, and local token estimates.

ProviderCacheTraceSegment.description: A content-free fingerprint of one provider-visible prompt segment. These records are safe to keep in the compact conversation projection: they retain enough structure to explain cache-prefix changes without persisting prompt text, tool output, or image bytes a second time.

kind.description: Legacy preset identity for older desktop builds.

ProviderInstructionEncoding.description: Deterministic instruction lowering selected during capability negotiation. The adapter reads this value while encoding; it never probes or changes it.

ProviderKind.description: Legacy provider preset identity. New runtime code resolves transport, authentication, and adapter independently; this enum remains serialized for one compatibility window so older desktop builds can still read settings.

oneOf.description: Delegate model execution and local file attachments to an installed Codex App Server instance.

ProviderMessageProtocolCapabilities.description: Assistant-message constraints imposed by one concrete wire protocol. These are negotiated or supplied by a trusted built-in endpoint contract; request codecs consume the result without inspecting vendor or model names.

requiresReasoningContentForToolCalls.description: Every assistant message that contains tool calls must preserve the provider-issued `reasoning_content` field in subsequent requests.

supportsVision.description: Image-input support reported by the provider's model catalog. `None` means the endpoint did not publish modality metadata for this model.

preferredAdapter.description: Optional model-level protocol preference. This is independent from the connection preset and may be overridden again by a thread selection.

supportsVision.description: An explicit user choice that takes precedence over catalog detection.

temperature.description: Outer `None` inherits the legacy connection setting. Inner `None` explicitly omits the request parameter for this model.

ProviderOutputProtocolCapabilities.description: Structured final-output features exposed by one concrete wire protocol. These are negotiated during provider setup and never inferred by retrying a modified request after a live turn has already started.

ProviderReasoningProtocol.description: Structural request envelope used to control model reasoning. Variant names describe wire behavior rather than vendors or model families. Capability negotiation owns this choice; request codecs never infer it from a model id.

adapterProfiles.description: Negotiated wire contract per model. This is the sole runtime source for adapter selection and message lowering; probe reports are diagnostics.

allowedAdapters.description: Protocols this connection is permitted to use. Empty is a legacy value and is interpreted from `kind` until settings are next saved.

contextWindowTokens.description: Optional user override. When omitted, the server resolves a known model capability and falls back to a conservative default for custom models.

enabledFamilies.description: Model families the user allowed for this connection. Empty means "not narrowed yet", which shows every synced family rather than none.

kind.description: Deprecated preset identity retained only for serialized compatibility. Runtime dispatch must use `effective_transport`, `effective_auth`, and `resolved_adapter_for_model` instead.

model.description: Default model for this connection. Threads may override it per conversation; this value is the fallback for new threads and for internal utility calls such as title generation.

modelCapabilities.description: Capabilities reported for each model by the connection's catalog.

modelContextWindows.description: Context windows the connection reported for its own models. Populated on sync when the endpoint publishes them, which is the only real capability detection available; it outranks the built-in table.

modelSettings.description: Per-model user overrides. These are intentionally separate from the catalog so a subsequent sync never discards an explicit choice.

name.description: User-facing label. Empty values from legacy settings fall back to `id`.

openaiCompatibility.description: Last explicit compatibility probe for an OpenAI-compatible `/v1` connection. The endpoint and model are included so stale results are ignored after either setting changes.

preferredAdapter.description: Connection-wide preference. `None` means use model preference, then the latest probe recommendation, then the legacy preset fallback.

syncedModels.description: Model ids last returned by the connection's `/v1/models` endpoint. Cached so the picker works offline; refreshed on explicit sync.

temperature.description: `None` means "don't send temperature — let the model use its default." This is important for reasoning models (o-series, GPT-5.x) that reject explicit temperature, and for users who want the vendor default.

ProviderToolProtocolCapabilities.description: Capabilities of the selected API protocol as actually exposed by a connection. `Unknown` intentionally behaves like unsupported at selection time so compatible relays always retain the portable function-tool path.

deferredToolLoading.description: Function definitions may be advertised with `defer_loading`.

hostedToolSearch.description: The provider can execute the hosted `tool_search` tool.

hostedWebSearch.description: The endpoint/model can execute the Responses hosted `web_search` tool. Compatible relays must prove this independently from function tools.

namespaceTools.description: Deferred functions may be grouped under native namespaces.

parallelToolCalls.description: The protocol accepts the optional `parallel_tool_calls` request hint.

streamingTools.description: The selected adapter/model/endpoint tuple has passed a production-codec round trip with tools enabled and streaming transport selected. Unknown is deliberately treated as unsupported when preparing a tool-capable request.

RuntimeConnectionAuthorityV1.description:
Frozen authority for external Connection operations.

This discriminator is independent from collaboration snapshots because the same immutable authority is also owned by persisted Flow runs. In particular, `structured { operations: [] }` is an explicit empty grant and must never fall back to mutable legacy thread MCP bindings.

modelSelection.description: Model chosen for this conversation. Pinned at creation so a catalog refresh never swaps the model mid-thread; `None` means "use the active connection's default", which keeps pre-existing threads working.

providerAdapter.description: Concrete protocol contract used by this thread snapshot.

providerKind.description: Deprecated connection preset retained for event compatibility.

ThreadModelSelection.description: A concrete model to run a thread with. The connection supplies the endpoint and credentials; this only narrows which model and how hard it thinks.

TokenEstimateBreakdown.description:
Provider-neutral estimate of the logical input carried by one model request.

These values are intentionally kept separate from provider-reported usage: they explain which harness modules built the request, while provider usage is the billing/accounting authority after the request completes.

deferredToolCatalog.description: Names/descriptions visible before a deferred tool is selected.

details.description: Hierarchical local attribution. Omitted when replaying legacy logs.

directToolSchemas.description: Full input schemas sent directly in the request's tool surface.

loadedToolSchemas.description: Schemas appended by a provider Tool Search continuation.

outputSchema.description: A structured-output schema is a request field, not a tool definition.

toolSchemas.description: Sum of the three tool-surface buckets above. Counted in `total` once.

turnAssistantState.description: Provider-native assistant message items replayed inside the active turn. These are neither durable conversation history nor opaque continuation state, so they remain a separate, mutually exclusive bucket.

TokenEstimateDetail.description:
One node in the local attribution tree for a logical model request.

Providers report request-level usage totals. These nodes preserve the harness-owned structure used to assemble that request without presenting the individual values as provider-billed facts.

metadata.description: Tool-specific metadata is also the forward-compatible place for context and artifact hints, such as truncated/originalBytes/maxResults.

output.description: Legacy text output. New tools should populate `content`; consumers can use `content_or_legacy_text` while callers migrate.

invocationId.description: Monotonic execution attempt inside this logical Turn. Interactive resumes increment this value without changing `turn_id`.

cancelled.description: Dismiss the decision boundary and end the waiting Turn without another model invocation. A later user message starts a new Turn normally.

skipped.description: Skip the optional decision and let the same Turn continue with a reasonable assumption.

windowId.description: Opaque, runtime-issued identifier. On Windows this is formatted from an HWND but callers must never synthesize it: `observe` verifies it against a live process before binding it.

resumeCommand.description: The command is retained after execution as an immutable audit record. It only applies when its interrupt id/revision matches `interrupt`.
